correctness.rationale: For σ²>0, n≥2 and admissible T=h(Y), centered Gaussian Y lives on a d=n−1-dimensional isotropic subspace, so Y=σ R U with independent R~χ_d and uniform direction U. Positive q-homogeneity gives h(Y)=σ^q R^q h(U); under size bias the joint law still factorizes. The χ_d radial density r^{d−1}e^(−r²/2) is multiplied by r^q and becomes exactly χ_{d+q}, including noninteger q. Hence dS²/σ²=R² is χ²_{d+q} under the biased law; the Laplace and gamma-moment formulas follow. Its first moment gives Cov(T,S²)=q σ² ET/d. Sample range and Gini difference depend only on Y and are nonnegative degree one. The proof works without smoothness, even for d=1 and q=0. Finite source code checks integer and fractional gamma moments but does not supply the universal factorization.

value.rationale: Provides an exact universal sampling law under a natural weighting operation, not only one new correlation: every χ² mixed moment under bias follows simultaneously for nonsmooth, nonparametric angular statistics. The covariance identity for sample range and Gini difference is an immediately useful, precisely motivated consequence; it is not presented as a new gamma-tilt method.

limitations: Requires positive normal σ² and residual-only nonnegative homogeneous T with finite positive mean.
Only the radial law is universal; biased angular distribution depends on h and joint law of other components is not claimed.
